chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Malik, who said:

I wrote to him: A man died and made everything of his during his lifetime, to be for you, and there was no child for him. Then a child was born (after his death) and his wealth had reached three thousand Dirham, and I had sent to you a thousand Dirhams. May I be sacrificed for you, So if you could let me know your view with regards to it, so that I can act upon it. So he wrote: 'I leave it for them'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to an estate if a child is born after the father's death when the will designated everything to someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia juristic principle that a child born after the testator's death is considered an heir and takes precedence over a specific bequest (*wasiyya*) to a non-heir, provided the estate exceeds the one-third limit for bequests. The Imam’s directive to 'release it to them' underscores the priority of *nasab* (lineage) in inheritance distribution, ensuring the posthumous child secures their obligatory share before the beneficiary claims the remainder.
